title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §3 from the previous page. Grothendieck is constructing the universal pair (B, J_B) with a divided-power (PD) ideal receiving a ring map u : A → B with u(J) ⊂ J_B. In modern terms this is the PD envelope of (A, J), with no compatibility condition imposed.

1. Start from J viewed as an A-module and form the augmentation ideal Γ⁺_A(J) of its divided power algebra. Γ⁺_A(J) is a PD-algebra over A, but it forgets that J is closed under multiplication.

2. Divide by the ideal generated by the elements (x·y)^{(n)} − x^n * y^{(n)}. Here '.' is the multiplication of J (inside A) and '*' is the multiplication of Γ⁺_A(J). Call the quotient J'. These relations encode the PD axiom γ_n(xy) = x^n γ_n(y), which also forces the A-module action of x ∈ J on J' to agree with multiplication by its image x'.

3. Grothendieck notes that the operations π_n pass to the quotient. So J' is a non-unital A-algebra with divided powers. He remarks that this construction is needed precisely because J is an ideal of A and not just a module.

4. Glue A and J' along J. Give A × J' the square-zero-type ring structure (a,ξ)(b,η) = (ab, aη + bξ + ξη). Then form the quotient A × J' / α(J), where α(x) = (x, −x') and x ↦ x' is the canonical map J → J'. He checks that α(J) is an ideal: (a,ξ)(x,−x') = (ax, −(ax)') once xξ = x'ξ in J'. He calls the result 'the extension of A/J by J''. The map J' → quotient is injective, so J' becomes a PD ideal of Γ(A,J) := A × J'/α(J), and A → Γ(A,J) is the universal arrow.

5. N.B.: if A is a Λ-algebra, then Γ(A,J) is a Λ-algebra through Λ → A → Γ(A,J).

Purpose: this is foundational material for crystalline cohomology. The PD envelope is what makes the crystalline site and De Rham comparison work. The next page computes the example Γ(Sym M, Sym⁺ M) ≅ Γ_Λ(M) and PD quotients.
errors: The ideal check is written sloppily as (a,ξ)(x,−x') = (ax, −ξx'). The correct product is (ax, −a x' + xξ − ξx'), which equals (ax, −(ax)') only after using xξ = x'ξ in J'. That identity is exactly what the relations of step 2 guarantee, so the argument is fine but compressed.
The notation x^n in the relation must be read in Γ⁺_A(J) (i.e. x^{[1]*n} = n! x^{[n]}), not as the power x^n ∈ J. As written this is ambiguous but harmless.

ideas.what: Construction of the universal PD-ideal receiving (A,J): quotient of Γ⁺_A(J) by the relations (xy)^{[n]} = x^n y^{[n]}, then gluing with A along J
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (Les algèbres à puissances divisées, 1965); Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407, 1974), Ch. I §2.3
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; the standard reference is Berthelot's thesis, based on Grothendieck's program and these notes' setting

ideas.what: Ring A × J'/α(J) as the 'extension of A/J by J''
ideas.modern_name: Pushout / gluing of a ring along an ideal map (Milnor-type square)

ideas.what: Λ-algebra structure on Γ(A,J) induced by Λ → A
ideas.modern_name: base change / functoriality of PD envelopes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard construction of the divided power envelope, already in Roby (1965) and Berthelot (1974). The only distinctive feature is the two-step route (first make J' a PD-algebra, then glue it to A). It is a minor presentational variant, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'J^\flat' in α : J^\flat → A × J' is almost certainly just J (α : J → A × J').

'yegen [?]' after the product formula is illegible; likely a short note such as 'etc.' or a gloss. The formula itself should read (a,ξ)(x,−x') = (ax, −ξx') as written, though mathematically it needs the term −a x'.

The opening '[-...-] {+produit+} anneau à puissances divisées' probably reads 'divisé{+es+}' with an insertion above 'anneau'. Likely sense: '[on considère le quotient de Γ⁺_A(J)] anneau à puissances divisées par l'idéal engendré par...'.
'construction redéfinissant [?] du fois [?] que J était un idéal de A' likely reads 'construction rendue nécessaire du fait que J était un idéal de A'.
